newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares - bull charges again, testing records.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares - bull charges again, testing records.

text.p: Russian shares tested records on Friday as Western investors leapt back into the stock market with high expectations, traders said.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index firmed to 251.07 from 243.31 -- just shy of a record 251.49. Total market volume was also just below a record at $54.3 million.

"People are anticipating a new and improved Yeltsin on the scene," said Peter Kizenko, chief equities trader at ING Barings, who said U.S. support late on Thursday had reinvigorated the market, stalled in the middle of this week.
After the Russian market closed on Thursday a Kremlin doctor said the condition of President Boris Yeltsin, in hospital with pneumonia, had stabilised.
After the market closed on Friday, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin was likely to leave hospital in the next few days, but not at the weekend.
"I don't see why we can't double the year's gains to date over the next couple of months," said Kizenko.

UCB's securities director Dmitry Yevenko said investors had scooped up stocks which had underperformed in the recent bull market, among them Rostelekom, which firmed to $2.70 from $2.53 at Thursday's close.
UES, which has not been ignored in recent weeks, hit $0.1408 during the day but eased to close at $0.1377 on Thursday's $0.1325.
Traders said leading stocks led the bull charge and were seen continuing to do well in a tight market where high liquidity was valued.
"As much as people want to be patient (to buy stock at lower prices) there just isn't time to be," Kizenko said.
